subject: Medford Square District Improvement Financing and Election Ballot Errors
overview: The City Council approved the District Improvement Financing ordinance for Medford Square and addressed reports of duplicate mail-in ballots being sent to residents. The body also discussed traffic mitigation strategies for neighborhood streets and light sequences on state-managed roads.

items.title: Recognition and Meeting Records
items.summary: Congratulated Henry and Evelyn Miller for their decades of service to the Arc of Massachusetts and individuals with disabilities, and approved the minutes of the October 17 meeting.

items.title: 23-412: 12 Dell Avenue Deed Restriction
items.summary: Tabled a petition to remove a deed restriction at 12 Dell Avenue until November 28 to allow for further negotiations between the petitioner and city departments.

items.title: 23-442: Willis Avenue Traffic Mitigation
items.summary: Referred a resolution to the Traffic Commission to review speed tables and one-way traffic adjustments to reduce cut-through volume on Willis Avenue. Residents and councilors emphasized that regional gridlock and navigation apps have increasingly pushed traffic onto neighborhood streets.

items.title: 23-443: State-Managed Traffic Light Sequences
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting that the DCR and the city traffic engineer adjust light timing at Fulton Street, the Fellsway, and Winthrop Street to improve public safety and traffic flow.

items.title: 23-419: Medford Square District Improvement Financing (DIF)
items.summary: Passed the District Improvement Financing ordinance on third reading, establishing a fund to capture tax revenue from new development to pay for infrastructure and revitalization projects in Medford Square.

items.title: 23-444: Election Ballot Distribution Errors
items.summary: Discussed reports of duplicate mail-in ballots sent to a small percentage of voters; officials clarified that state-assigned unique identifiers prevent more than one ballot being counted per person. Councilors expressed concern that staffing reductions in the elections department contributed to recent printing and distribution errors.

items.title: Public Participation
items.summary: Andrew Castagnetti spoke on various infrastructure concerns, including the Mystic River bike path and the Kristin Campbell fountain; Linda Colozzo requested council assistance regarding outstanding cost-of-living and COVID-related pay for former city employees.
